canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.name: Mekong Delta Chicken and Lá Cách Soup
aliases: Vietnamese chicken and lá cách soup
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.serving_basis: One shared dish for four at a family meal.
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.description: Chicken pieces simmer with lemongrass and garlic, then fresh lá cách leaves are added at the end for their warm, distinctive aroma. Bếp Việt standardizes the family-sized seasoning from a Mekong Delta recipe reference and keeps the leaves briefly cooked.
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.finished_dish: The chicken is tender yet firm, the broth is clear and savory, and the briefly cooked leaves retain their distinctive fragrance.
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice. Pair with boiled greens or a simply braised dish to balance the leaves’ assertive aroma.
tips: Choose tender lá cách leaves, rinse gently and drain; prolonged cooking can darken them and intensify their pungency.
Bone-in free-range chicken works well; check that the meat is fully cooked near the bone before serving.
Seasoning quantities are Bếp Việt’s editorial adaptation; adjust fish sauce and chili to taste.
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.image_alt: A serving bowl of hot chicken and lá cách soup with chicken pieces, green leaves and lemongrass, isolated on a transparent background.
canh-ga-la-cach-mien-tay.time_note: About 55 minutes sequentially; marinating or soaking time is listed separately.

ingredients.name: Bone-in free-range chicken, cut into pieces
ingredients.notes: Use thighs, wings or mixed bone-in pieces.

ingredients.name: Lá cách leaves
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves and rinse well.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise and cut into lengths.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice; optional.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between marinating and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add gradually.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to balance the flavor.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the aromatics.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust so the chicken is just covered.

preparation_steps: Rinse and drain the chicken, then cut into serving pieces. Marinate for 10 minutes with 5 ml of the fish sauce, half the garlic and a pinch of salt.
Gently rinse the lá cách leaves and remove tough stems; bruise the lemongrass, mince the remaining garlic and slice the chili.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the remaining garlic with the lemongrass until fragrant. Add the chicken and turn until the surface is sealed.
Add the water, bring to a boil, lower the heat, skim the foam and simmer for about 20–25 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Season with the remaining fish sauce, salt and sugar. Add the lá cách leaves and chili, simmer for 2–3 minutes, then turn off the heat.

vit-rang-muoi.name: Vietnamese Salt-Roasted Duck
aliases: Crispy duck with roasted rice seasoning
vit-rang-muoi.serving_basis: One shared dish for four at a family meal.
vit-rang-muoi.description: Crisp fried duck is tossed briefly with lemongrass and a toasted seasoning made from rice, glutinous rice and mung beans. Bếp Việt standardizes a family-sized batch and keeps the coating light so it tastes nutty rather than overly salty.
vit-rang-muoi.finished_dish: The duck is golden and crisp outside while remaining juicy inside, with fragrant lemongrass and a lightly savory, nutty salt coating.
vit-rang-muoi.serving: Serve hot with fresh herbs, cucumber and steamed rice; offer lime and chili separately if serving as a snack.
tips: Use a deep pan and fry in batches so the oil temperature stays steady; cook the duck completely through.
Toast the rice, glutinous rice and mung beans separately over low heat before grinding; do not let them scorch.
Add only enough seasoning powder to coat the duck lightly; keep any extra aside.
vit-rang-muoi.image_alt: A plate of golden salt-roasted duck topped with crisp lemongrass and toasted seasoning, isolated on a transparent background.
vit-rang-muoi.time_note: About 85 minutes sequentially; marinating or soaking time is listed separately.

ingredients.name: Duck, cut into pieces
ingredients.notes: Pat dry after cleaning.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly and drain.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly and drain.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Use dried split beans.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper

ingredients.name: Egg

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil

preparation_steps: Rub the duck with bruised ginger and rice wine, rinse and pat dry, then cut into serving pieces.
Rinse the glutinous rice, rice and mung beans; soak for 15 minutes and drain thoroughly. Slice the lemongrass into thin strips and beat the egg.
cooking_steps: Toast the glutinous rice, rice and mung beans separately over low heat until golden and fragrant. Dry-toast the coarse salt, cool, then grind it with the grains.
Marinate the duck with fish sauce and pepper for 15 minutes. Dip each piece in egg, then coat lightly with tapioca starch.
Heat the oil and fry the duck in batches until golden and cooked through; drain. Fry the lemongrass strips until fragrant and golden, then remove.
Leave a thin film of oil in the pan. Toss the duck with the lemongrass and gradually add the roasted seasoning, just enough to coat; remove from the heat.

vit-xao-lan.name: Vietnamese Duck Stir-Braised with Lemongrass
aliases: Duck xào lăn with coconut water
vit-xao-lan.serving_basis: One shared dish for four at a family meal.
vit-xao-lan.description: Duck is marinated with five-spice, lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, seared, then gently braised with fresh coconut water until the sauce reduces. Bếp Việt retains the method documented by Vĩnh Long Newspaper and standardizes quantities for four, without claiming the dish belongs exclusively to one region.
vit-xao-lan.finished_dish: The duck is tender and firm with fragrant lemongrass and five-spice; reduced coconut water forms a lightly sweet-savory glaze.
vit-xao-lan.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, black pepper and chili to taste. Fresh greens or cucumber balance the rich seasoning.
tips: Allow time for the duck to absorb the marinade; keep it refrigerated during a long rest.
Sear the duck over high heat until browned before adding coconut water.
Simmer gently and uncover near the end to reduce the sauce without scorching the natural sugars.
vit-xao-lan.image_alt: A plate of glossy Vietnamese duck stir-braised with lemongrass, chili and reduced coconut water, isolated on a transparent background.
vit-xao-lan.time_note: About 170 minutes sequentially; marinating or soaking time is listed separately.

ingredients.name: Boneless duck, cut into pieces
ingredients.notes: Thigh meat works well; cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Bruise for cleaning the duck.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water

ingredients.name: Lemongrass

ingredients.name: Shallot

ingredients.name: Garlic

ingredients.name: Fresh chili

ingredients.name: Five-spice powder

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and final seasoning.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the sweetness of the coconut water.

ingredients.name: Salt

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper

preparation_steps: Rub the duck with salt and ginger, rinse, drain and cut into bite-size pieces.
Mince the lemongrass, shallot, garlic and chili. Toss the duck with five-spice, fish sauce, sugar, salt, half the lemongrass, shallot and garlic; marinate under refrigeration for about 2 hours.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the remaining lemongrass, shallot and garlic until fragrant. Add the duck and marinade; stir-fry over high heat until the meat is sealed.
Add the coconut water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 15–20 minutes until the duck is tender and cooked through.
Uncover and toss until the sauce reduces to a light glaze. Adjust with the remaining fish sauce, chili and pepper; remove from the heat when balanced.

goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.name: Vegetarian Thiên Lý Flower Salad
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.serving_basis: One shared dish for four at a family meal.
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.description: Quick-blanched thiên lý flowers keep their vivid green color and are tossed with carrot, pineapple, mint and plant-based protein in a tangy-sweet dressing. Bếp Việt edits the documented vegetarian salad into a fully plant-based version, using a coconut-pineapple-soy dressing.
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.finished_dish: The thiên lý flowers are tender-crisp, carrot and pineapple stay fresh, plant protein carries the tangy-sweet dressing, and peanuts add crunch.
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.serving: Toss shortly before serving, then top with roasted peanuts and mint. Serve with vegetarian rice crackers or steamed rice.
tips: Blanch the flowers only until they turn bright green, then cool them quickly to preserve their texture.
Choose clearly labelled plant-based protein; any crackers served alongside must contain no shrimp or other animal ingredients.
The dressing is Bếp Việt’s variation and contains no fish sauce; balance the sweet and sour elements gradually.
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.image_alt: A fresh green thiên lý flower salad with carrot, pineapple, plant-based protein and roasted peanuts, isolated on a transparent background.
goi-bong-thien-ly-chay.time_note: About 48 minutes sequentially; marinating or soaking time is listed separately.

ingredients.name: Thiên lý flowers
ingredients.notes: Remove tough stems and rinse gently.

ingredients.name: Sliced plant-based meat

ingredients.name: Plant-based shrimp
ingredients.notes: Check the ingredients contain no real shrimp.

ingredients.name: Carrot

ingredients.name: Pineapple

ingredients.name: Mint

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly; fry half until golden.

ingredients.name: Pickled shallot
ingredients.notes: Chop finely; check for fish ingredients.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the leek.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush coarsely and add at the end.

ingredients.name: Calamansi or lime juice
ingredients.notes: Strain out the seeds.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: For the coconut dressing.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a vegan soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the tartness of the fruit.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For blanching and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Mince; reduce or omit to taste.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian crackers
ingredients.notes: Use a product labelled fully plant-based.

preparation_steps: Pick over and rinse the thiên lý flowers. Cut the carrot and pineapple, slice the leek, pick the mint leaves and crush the roasted peanuts.
Blanch the plant-based meat and shrimp in boiling water for 1–2 minutes, then drain; check product labels to ensure they are fully plant-based.
Mix part of the sugar with the calamansi or lime juice, toss with the carrot and let it stand for about 15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Blanch the flowers in lightly salted boiling water for 45–60 seconds, transfer to ice water, then drain thoroughly.
Bring the coconut water, pineapple juice, soy sauce and remaining sugar to a gentle boil; cool, then stir in the calamansi or lime juice.
Sauté half the leek in a little oil, briefly warm the plant-based meat and shrimp, then let them cool.
Combine the flowers, carrot, pineapple, plant protein, pickled shallot, chili and mint in a bowl. Add the dressing gradually and toss gently; adjust to taste, top with peanuts and serve immediately.

rau-cu-kho-chay.name: Vietnamese Vegetarian Braised Vegetables
rau-cu-kho-chay.serving_basis: One shared dish for four at a family meal.
rau-cu-kho-chay.description: Tofu, mushrooms and familiar vegetables are gently braised in coconut water with lemongrass for a naturally sweet, colorful dish. Bếp Việt standardizes a four-person batch from a reference recipe and adds eggplant and okra later so they keep their shape.
rau-cu-kho-chay.finished_dish: The vegetables are tender but hold their shape, while mushrooms and tofu absorb the seasoning; the coconut-based sauce is lightly thick and fragrant with lemongrass.
rau-cu-kho-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or plain rice porridge. Portion gently so the vegetables stay intact; the dish is best while they still hold their shape.
tips: Cut the vegetables evenly so they cook at a similar rate; avoid vigorous stirring while braising.
Season gradually because the coconut water becomes more concentrated as it reduces.
Add eggplant and okra toward the end so they do not become mushy.
rau-cu-kho-chay.image_alt: A colorful Vietnamese braise of vegetables, tofu, mushrooms and a light coconut sauce, isolated on a transparent background.
rau-cu-kho-chay.time_note: About 60 minutes sequentially; marinating or soaking time is listed separately.

preparation_steps: Rinse the mushrooms, carrot, pineapple, baby corn, okra and green beans; prepare the eggplant last to limit browning. Cut the ingredients into evenly sized pieces.
Toss the tofu, mushrooms, carrot, baby corn and green beans with the soy sauce, sugar and salt. Let them absorb the seasoning for about 5 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the lemongrass until fragrant. Add the seasoned vegetables and turn gently for 2–3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut water, bring to a boil, lower the heat and braise for about 15 minutes.
Add the eggplant, okra and pineapple; braise for another 8–10 minutes until just tender. Adjust the seasoning, turn off the heat and finish with pepper.
